title.narrative: Human Immunodeficiency Virus Infection/Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (HIV/AIDS) Prevention Among Youth

description.narrative: The objective of the Project is to reduce HIV/AIDS infection rates among young people (15-24 years old). To achieve this, the Project will support the Government to implement a comprehensive behavior change communication program aimed at reducing HIV/AIDS infection risk for youth. The Project will have four components: (1) leadership and strategy support for HIV/AIDS prevention among youth; (2) a national mass media program for behavior change; (3) community-based HIV/AIDS prevention resources for youth including harm reduction outreach services, HIV prevention for vulnerable youth, and primary prevention programs for youth and families; and (4) project management, capacity building, monitoring, and evaluation.

description.narrative: HIV infection risk behaviors reduced among youth aged 15-24 years

1. Increase in condom use at last high-risk sex Progress/Status: Condom use at the last intercourse among vulnerable groups increased from base to end-line surveys. Data Source: AIDS Indicator Survey IBBS Project completion report Baseline value: N

2. Increase in percentage of young people identifyinig a formal source of condoms Progress/Status: IBBS 2009 showed the increase of consistent condom use among IDU in most provinces, including project provinces. For example, the proportion of IDU using condoms with FSW in Hanoi is 52% in 2005 and 60.6% in 2009, in Can Tho from 47% to 56.9% (IBBS 2009). In general, the percentage of male IDU to use condoms at last sexual intercourse increased by 70%, from 36.4% in 2006 to 51.9% in 2009 (UNGASS 2008, 2010) Data Source: AIDS Indicator Survey IBBS Project completion report Baseline value: N

3. Increase in percentage of population aged 15-24 years with comprehensive correct knowledge of HIV/AIDS Progress/Status: The data in end-line survey has the same result, that general knowledge about HIV/AIDS among IDUs, FSWs, and migrant workers was improved. The changes in each of these items at baseline and end line respectively were: HIV can be transmitted through sex (84.7% to 86.3%), HIV can be transmitted from mother to baby (61% to 67%), and HIV can be transmitted through blood/syringe (58% to 75.7%). Data Source: AIDS Indicator Survey IBBS Project completion report Baseline value: N

4. From baseline measure, needle-sharing among IDUs reduced by 20% in project provinces by end of project Progress/Status: The proportion of IDU to “use syringe and needle that other had used” reduced from 39.4% to 16.1%, “squirt drug solution from your syringe to someone else's syringe” (45% to 25.9%) and “giving other syringe and needle after you had used” (36.4% to 29.5%) (PCR of PMU) Data Source: AIDS Indicator Survey IBBS Project completion report Baseline value: N

The assessment of impacts by the mass media campaign will be conducted. Component 3: In project provinces, an increase in the percentage of youth with access to HIV harm-reduction and prevention education programs, including through outreach services, peereducation and community-based education programs Indicator: From first episode, steadily increasing and maintained viewer numbers for TV drama series; percentage of youth in vulnerable and mainstream situations who reject major misconceptions about common HIV transmission routes and condom use (footnote d) Progress/Status: The drama has been aired on the national and provincial Television. Based on media surveys, the public appreciation was mixed. The PMU will collect evidence of impact of the drama series. The weekly radio phone-in program “60 minutes you and me”, after almost 2 years of airing, became a popular program for the youth in the project provinces. Besides, 90 thematic TV spots, radio spots, 6 documentary films, and complete set of interpersonal communication materials targeting mainstream youth, illegal drug users (IDUs), sex workers, parents and leaders; writing competition on HIV/AIDS was organized for youth and students.

NGOs (MSI and CCRD) have been contracted to implement harm reduction activities in the provinces. They help set up VTC sites and train health staff and peer educators. Data Source: Annual report with service data from NGOs implementing harmreduction services gender disaggregated)
